Lieutenants
lū-tĕn´ănts
n. pl. (the Persian satraps; the king's deputies over the provinces)
Old French lieu tenant, place-holder — one who holds a place in another's stead. The KJV uses it for the Persian achashdarpan, the satrap of an imperial province.

Biblical Definition

Ezra carries the king's authority into hostile country: “they delivered the king's commissions unto the king's lieutenants, and to the governors on this side the river: and they furthered the people, and the house of God” (Ezr 8:36). Esther records the same officials on the day the tables turned: “all the rulers of the provinces, and the lieutenants, and the deputies, and officers of the king, helped the Jews; because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them” (Est 9:3) — the man they now feared having been, a short time before, paraded through the street by the enemy who built his gallows (Est 6:11).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a lieutenant as an officer who supplies the place of a superior in his absence; one who acts by vicarious authority.

expand to see more

LIEUTENANT, n. An officer who supplies the place of a superior in his absence; a deputy.

LIEUTENANT, n. In military affairs, the second commissioned officer in a company of infantry, cavalry or artillery.

DEPUTY, n. A person appointed or elected to act for another; a substitute in office.

Key Scripture

Ezr 8:36 — "And they delivered the king's commissions unto the king's lieutenants, and to the governors on this side the river: and they furthered the people, and the house of God."

Est 6:11 — "Then took Haman the apparel and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai, and brought him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaimed before him, Thus shall it be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour."

Est 8:15 — "And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad."

Est 9:3 — "And all the rulers of the provinces, and the lieutenants, and the deputies, and officers of the king, helped the Jews; because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them."

Modern Corruption

Persian officials furthered the house of God and helped the Jews, which is how Scripture describes God governing His people through a bureaucracy that never knew Him.

expand to see more

Ezra and Esther are the books of the hidden hand. There is no pillar of fire in either, no prophet doing signs, no army of the LORD. There are commissions, satraps, letters sealed with the king's ring, a sleepless night, and a book of records read aloud. And through that machinery the house of God is built and a nation is preserved. Ezra says it plainly — the hand of our God is upon all them for good that seek him — and then describes the good arriving in the form of a Persian filing system. Esther never mentions God's name and is about nothing else.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that providence is usually administrative. Believers are trained by the dramatic passages of Scripture to look for deliverance shaped like the Red Sea, and most deliverance in Scripture, and nearly all of it in ordinary life, looks like Ezra 8:36 — officials who furthered the people, for reasons of their own, at the right moment. The prayer of Ezra 8:21, fasting at the river Ahava for a right way, was answered by a safe road and cooperative civil servants. That is not a lesser answer.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew achashdarpan (H323), satrap, lieutenant of a Persian province; pechah (H6346), governor; dath (H1881), decree, commission.

expand to see more

Hebrew achashdarpan (H323) — satrap, lieutenant; Ezra 8:36, Esther 3:12, 8:9, 9:3.

Hebrew pechah (H6346) — governor, deputy; Ezra 8:36, Nehemiah 5:14.

Hebrew dath (H1881) — decree, law, commission; Ezra 8:36, Esther 1:19.

Hebrew nasa (H5375) — to lift up, further, support; Ezra 8:36, 1:4.

Hebrew pachad (H6343) — fear, dread; Esther 9:3, Genesis 31:42.

Usage

"“They furthered the people, and the house of God” — Persian officials, God's purpose."

"“The lieutenants, and the deputies, and officers of the king, helped the Jews.”"

"“Because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them” — the reason given."
